nodes.label: Manu · guardian of the Sun Oracle

edges.claim: The Thrones provide the initial substance for the physical human germ. Other hierarchies work over what they give.
edges.qualification: The germ is described through warmth, long before the dense organism of Earth.

edges.claim: The Spirits of Wisdom impart the life body, bringing inner life to the inherited physical germ.
edges.qualification: The physical germ continues to develop as the etheric organization is added.

edges.claim: The Spirits of Movement impart the astral body to the inherited physical and etheric organizations.
edges.qualification: The earlier members are prepared through a renewed working of the preceding conditions.

edges.claim: The Spirits of Form fashion the independent human I during Earth evolution.
edges.qualification: The I enters an already layered organization and can subsequently work on its members.

edges.claim: After an interval, what was attained on Saturn reappears at the beginning of the Sun condition before life is imparted.
edges.qualification: The earlier achievement is reworked in a new setting.

edges.claim: Following cosmic sleep, the Moon condition renews the inherited organization before the new astral activity.
edges.qualification: The source describes both the rest in outer activity and the return of previous acquisitions.

edges.claim: The three inherited members must be prepared for the object-consciousness of Earth after an interval of rest.
edges.qualification: Their earlier organization supported picture-consciousness.

edges.claim: Steiner describes successive early Earth reprises of earlier conditions before specifically Earth development.
edges.qualification: These are transformed recapitulations on the scale of cosmic embodiments.

edges.claim: External activity gives way to a more spiritual interval before the next embodiment.
edges.qualification: Steiner distinguishes absence from ordinary observation and absence of all activity.

edges.claim: Earth passes through an intermediate spiritual condition before becoming Future Jupiter.
edges.qualification: GA 13 describes accompanying changes in kingdoms and a later solar separation.

edges.claim: A renewed solar union after a Jupiter separation precedes Future Venus.
edges.qualification: These names denote future conditions of the whole evolution.

edges.claim: Evolved humanity advances through a spiritualized existence into Future Vulcan.
edges.qualification: GA 13 explicitly leaves detailed description of Vulcan outside its scope.

edges.claim: Old Moon consciousness is characterized by living images.
edges.qualification: Steiner uses dreaming as a comparison and distinguishes the range and vitality of the experiences.

edges.claim: Steiner projects the emergence of consciously experienced image consciousness on Jupiter.
edges.qualification: The future formulation has a different degree of self-awareness from Old Moon.

edges.claim: Steiner characterizes Venus consciousness as Inspiration, using tone to describe access to inner character.
edges.qualification: This is a projected condition in the Apocalypse lecture.

edges.claim: Steiner characterizes the seventh condition through Intuition and entry into the being perceived.
edges.qualification: GA 104 supplies a consciousness characterization where GA 13 gives little detail.

edges.claim: Steiner compares the predominant Saturn condition to trance, deeper than dreamless sleep.
edges.qualification: He makes room for changes within the embodiment.

edges.claim: Dreamless sleep is the comparison for the characteristic Old Sun consciousness.
edges.qualification: The comparison concerns degree of consciousness.

edges.claim: Earth develops bright daytime or object consciousness.
edges.qualification: The same lecture differentiates seven life states and seven forms within each major consciousness state.

edges.claim: GA 13 traces a germ of Spirit-Man to the later part of Old Saturn.
edges.qualification: A germ and the later conscious work of the I are different developmental relations.

edges.claim: GA 13 places a germ of Life-Spirit on Old Sun.
edges.qualification: The statement leaves later maturation open.

edges.claim: GA 13 describes the formation of a germ of Spirit-Self during Old Moon.
edges.qualification: This refers to a preliminary germ.

edges.context: Higher members in the seven embodiments
edges.claim: Steiner places the development of Manas on Jupiter in his outline of human evolution.
edges.qualification: The same member has an earlier seed and can be anticipated at earlier stages.

edges.context: Higher members in the seven embodiments
edges.claim: Steiner places the development of Buddhi on Venus in this outline.
edges.qualification: Compare the Old Sun seed and the individual work described in GA 13 II.

edges.context: Higher members in the seven embodiments
edges.claim: Steiner places the development of Atma on Vulcan in this outline.
edges.qualification: GA 13 VI gives only a general account of arrival at Vulcan.

edges.claim: The Moon marks the outer extent of the Angeloi domain in this diagram.
edges.qualification: The domain runs outward from Earth in this presentation.

edges.claim: The esoteric Mercury marks the extent of the Archangeloi domain.
edges.qualification: Use the lecture’s terminology convention.

edges.claim: The esoteric Venus marks the extent associated with the Archai.
edges.qualification: GA 110 VII explicitly interchanges the physical labels Mercury and Venus.

edges.claim: The Sun marks the extent of the Spirits of Form, whose mission spans successive embodiments.
edges.qualification: A sphere boundary can coexist with participation by other hierarchies.

edges.claim: The Mars boundary is assigned to Spirits of Movement.
edges.qualification: Steiner uses nested regions of activity.

edges.claim: Jupiter marks the extent of the Spirits of Wisdom in the diagram.
edges.qualification: GA 136 gives Spirits of Wisdom a distinct role in general planetary constitution.

edges.claim: Saturn marks the extent of the Thrones in the hierarchy diagram.
edges.qualification: The reference is present Saturn as a spatial marker.

edges.claim: Saturn preserves and discloses the past of the planetary system.
edges.qualification: Read as Steiner’s description of spiritual perception.

edges.claim: Jupiter is described as the thinker of the planetary system, presenting the cosmic present in living ideas.
edges.qualification: The same lecture also associates Jupiter with the freedom to think.

edges.claim: Mars contributes to cosmic impulses for speech.
edges.qualification: GA 228 also brings Venus into the account of how speech comes about.

edges.claim: Venus is receptive to what lives in the depths of human souls and reflects it back.
edges.qualification: The context is the spiritual individuality of Venus.

edges.claim: Mercury works with Venus to deepen the soul-spiritual side of karma in disposition and temperament.
edges.qualification: Steiner distinguishes this from the Moon’s relation to heredity.

edges.claim: Steiner describes the Moon as the retreat of primeval teachers once active on Earth.
edges.qualification: The migration is part of his esoteric account.

edges.claim: GA 228 gives the Sun a mediating role between destiny-forming and freedom-enabling tendencies. GA 26 separately relates Christ to free human activity.
edges.qualification: The two lectures address different levels. This edge records the thematic connection.

edges.claim: Steiner says that beings including those he calls Vulcan beings have begun approaching earthly development.
edges.qualification: The lecture gives no proof that they are the agents of the earlier Oracle or inhabitants of Future Vulcan.

edges.claim: Jupiter bounds the Spirits of Wisdom in GA 110, and GA 13 assigns those spirits Old Sun etheric formation. GA 102 gives Jupiter beings an etheric role in a separately worded Earth narrative.
edges.qualification: Shared connections warrant a route through the sources, with each claim kept on its own scale.

edges.claim: Six Elohim act from the Sun in Steiner’s account of solar and lunar cooperation.
edges.qualification: The larger lecture contains historically racist classifications. This relationship concerns the selected cosmological passages.

edges.claim: Jehovah is the Elohim who makes the Moon his sphere of activity as the other six act from the Sun.
edges.qualification: Jehovah belongs to the Spirits of Form, while GA 110 gives the Angeloi a Moon boundary.

edges.claim: The Thrones or Spirits of Will provide the warmth-substance that grounds the human physical germ.
edges.qualification: The wider Saturn sequence involves additional hierarchies.

edges.claim: Steiner attributes the imparting of the etheric or life body to the Spirits of Wisdom.
edges.qualification: This is an Old Sun action.

edges.claim: Steiner attributes the imparting of the astral body to the Spirits of Motion.
edges.qualification: The same hierarchy has distinct functions elsewhere.

edges.claim: The Spirits of Form are the agents Steiner associates with independent I-hood.
edges.qualification: Steiner identifies freedom and love as capacities of the individual who develops through this organization.

edges.claim: The Angels passed through their corresponding human stage on Old Moon.
edges.qualification: Human stage here describes an attainment of the hierarchy.

edges.claim: The Archangels passed through their corresponding human stage on Old Sun.
edges.qualification: Their own attainment is distinct from the work of the Spirits of Wisdom on the human life body.

edges.claim: The Archai passed through their corresponding human stage on Old Saturn.
edges.qualification: They are also called Spirits of Personality.

edges.claim: Steiner assigns individual Angels the linking of successive human incarnations.
edges.qualification: The context concerns personal continuity through lives.

edges.claim: The Fire Spirits work on the etheric organization so the human being experiences continuity across renewals of bodily form.
edges.qualification: GA 13 describes this as a kind of memory, distinct from ordinary earthly recollection.

edges.claim: Steiner assigns the Spirits of Personality a role in developing independence of the astral body.
edges.qualification: This preparation precedes independent human I-hood on Earth.

edges.claim: The Sons of Life help make the physical body an expression of the astral.
edges.qualification: The shared spiritual guide in the Moon account has a group role.

edges.claim: The manifest shape of a planetary body is attributed to Spirits of Form in GA 136.
edges.qualification: This is a general contribution across planets.

edges.claim: Steiner attributes the inner mobility and life of a planet to Spirits of Movement.
edges.qualification: He distinguishes inner movement from change of position in space.

edges.claim: Steiner attributes a planet’s lowest consciousness to Spirits of Wisdom.
edges.qualification: He compares it with human astral consciousness.

edges.claim: The Thrones impart the impulse by which a planet changes position in space.
edges.qualification: Cherubim enter the same account at the level of coordinated motion.

edges.claim: The Cherubim coordinate a planet’s motion with the whole system and join the Seraphim in the account of light.
edges.qualification: This is a system-wide function.

edges.claim: Steiner ascribes to Seraphim the inner spiritual life by which planets enter into relations with other heavenly bodies.
edges.qualification: Human language is a comparison used in the lecture.

edges.claim: The Seraphim, Cherubim and Thrones anticipate or live through consequences in Steiner’s account of shaping karma.
edges.qualification: GA 239 describes their shared function and gives the solar Second Hierarchy a separate mediating role.

edges.claim: Cherubim are named with Seraphim and Thrones in the prospective working of karma.
edges.qualification: Steiner gives no one-planet assignment for this collective activity.

edges.claim: Thrones are named with Seraphim and Cherubim in the prospective working of karma.
edges.qualification: This role is separate from their Old Saturn formation of the human germ.

edges.claim: Steiner describes Spirit-Self as the astral body transformed through the I.
edges.qualification: The earlier germ and later conscious transformation are both represented.

edges.claim: Steiner describes Life-Spirit as transformation of the etheric body by the I.
edges.qualification: He distinguishes the slower and deeper transformation of life habits from ordinary intellectual change.

edges.claim: Steiner describes Spirit-Man as the I’s transformation of the physical organization.
edges.qualification: The referent is the spiritual activity underlying the body.

edges.claim: The astral body becomes Spirit-Self insofar as it is transformed through the I.
edges.qualification: The physical body, life body and astral body remain distinct starting points for transformation.

edges.claim: The transformation of the etheric body brings forth Life-Spirit.
edges.qualification: GA 13 treats the change as deeper than ordinary mental cultivation.

edges.claim: Work on the physical organization yields Spirit-Man in Steiner’s account.
edges.qualification: GA 13 places activity behind the visible bodily form.

edges.claim: The I comes to characteristic expression in the consciousness soul.
edges.qualification: The soul member and the activity of the I are distinguished.

edges.claim: Steiner associates the nerve-sense pole with ideation and alert consciousness.
edges.qualification: GA 21 treats activity functionally. The organization extends through the person.

edges.claim: Steiner relates feeling to rhythmic activity, with breathing as an example.
edges.qualification: The relationship is broader than any one organ.

edges.claim: Steiner relates willing to metabolism and action through the limbs.
edges.qualification: The source gives a conceptual account in Steiner’s physiology.

edges.claim: The waking I-organization engages part of warmth, and the astral organization also engages warmth within a different configuration.
edges.qualification: These lectures describe Steiner’s elemental and etheric framework.

edges.claim: In sleep astral body and I withdraw from their waking interpenetration with physical and etheric bodies.
edges.qualification: GA 317 III gives a more detailed account of waking re-engagement.

edges.claim: Steiner describes a panorama of memory while the etheric body loosens from the physical immediately after death.
edges.qualification: Keep separate from the creation of the memory faculty on the Saturn return in GA 231.

edges.claim: Steiner’s broad account combines an inaugural shaping with later contributions from different hierarchies.
edges.qualification: The layer model is a synthesis. Persistence varies by process and requires local evidence.

edges.claim: The Sun is Steiner’s image for the heart and circulation in his inner cosmic system.
edges.qualification: This is an occult organ analogy. It does not assert that a present astronomical body constructs the organ.

edges.claim: Steiner names the brain as the Moon of the inner cosmic system.
edges.qualification: GA 128 IV’s immediate enumeration does not include the brain.

edges.claim: Steiner calls the spleen’s activity Saturnian in the organ analogy.
edges.qualification: Compare the separate Saturn–liver influence statement in GA 102.

edges.claim: Steiner uses Jupiter to characterize the liver in the inner cosmic system.
edges.qualification: GA 102 I describes an additional Saturn relation using a different predicate.

edges.claim: Steiner calls the gallbladder Martian in the occult organ system.
edges.qualification: The comparison concerns relations within the system of organs.

edges.claim: Steiner uses Venus for the kidney system.
edges.qualification: The record preserves the author’s source-local label.

edges.claim: Steiner uses Mercury for the pulmonary system.
edges.qualification: The record preserves the author’s source-local label.

edges.claim: Steiner ascribes a strong influence of Saturn forces to the liver and connects that influence with the Prometheus myth.
edges.qualification: The German corroborates the pairing. How the influence relates to the Jovian designation remains open.

edges.claim: Steiner calls blood a principal physical expression of the I. GA 13 connects a first tendency toward blood circulation with inwardly experienced warmth.
edges.qualification: The doctrine concerns an expression in the body. Neither passage identifies a blood constituent as the I.

edges.claim: Steiner connects the nervous system with physical expression of the astral body.
edges.qualification: In GA 21 he approaches neural activity in a different framework, through its relationship to ideation.

edges.claim: Steiner names the glandular system as a bodily expression of the etheric body.
edges.qualification: Case-specific extensions of the lecture’s medical claims are outside this concordance.

edges.context: Inner organ analogy and threefold system
edges.claim: The cardiovascular solar analogy in GA 128 and the solar association with rhythm in GA 209 provide two routes into Steiner’s picture of bodily rhythm.
edges.qualification: The sources relate the Sun to different objects at different scales.

edges.claim: Steiner describes the bestowal of a macrocosmic spiritual heart in the second passage through the Sun sphere.
edges.qualification: The comparison with the bodily heartbeat in §20 does not make this the anatomical construction of the earthly heart.

edges.claim: Steiner associates the Moon with the forces of reproduction within the metabolic-limb pole.
edges.qualification: The statement is part of the 1921 spiritual physiology.

edges.claim: Mars beings participate in the formation of the sentient or feeling soul.
edges.qualification: This soul member has a wider meaning than the everyday faculty of feeling.

edges.claim: Steiner names Mercury in the development of the intellectual soul and separately as teacher of initiates.
edges.qualification: An earlier paragraph in the same lecture assigns intellectuality to Venus beings.

edges.claim: Jupiter beings stir the consciousness soul, with help from a category of Venus beings.
edges.qualification: The source emphasizes that planetary tasks change through evolution.

edges.claim: Steiner assigns Venus beings a role as Spirit-Self is drawn into the consciousness soul.
edges.qualification: This relation is distinct from Jupiter’s contribution to developing that soul member.

edges.claim: Steiner names Jupiter beings as earlier contributors to the etheric body and later to the consciousness soul.
edges.qualification: The earlier role is specified in the lecture’s own esoteric human chronology, distinct from GA 13’s Old Sun account.

edges.claim: Steiner describes Venus beings as endowing humans with intellectuality.
edges.qualification: Both checked English versions and German agree on the name. This is recorded separately from Mercury and the intellectual soul in §§23–24.

edges.claim: Jupiter’s grace is associated with the will impulse in free thinking.
edges.qualification: This is the 1923 account of planets enabling human freedom.

edges.claim: Saturn’s retention of cosmic memory and its contribution to free human remembering are related in GA 228.
edges.qualification: The journey account adds an explicit return-stage metamorphosis.

edges.context: Planetary activity in the threefold body
edges.claim: Steiner places the Sun at the middle of the planetary polarity and associates it chiefly with rhythmic activity.
edges.qualification: Compare the solar image for heart and circulation in GA 128.

edges.context: Planetary activity in the threefold body
edges.claim: Saturn is grouped with Jupiter and Mars at the consciousness pole.
edges.qualification: The claim concerns a functional pole.

edges.context: Planetary activity in the threefold body
edges.claim: Jupiter is grouped with Saturn and Mars at the consciousness pole.
edges.qualification: The Jovian liver analogy belongs to another scale.

edges.context: Planetary activity in the threefold body
edges.claim: Mars is grouped with Saturn and Jupiter at the consciousness pole.
edges.qualification: The gallbladder comparison uses a different relationship.

edges.context: Planetary activity in the threefold body
edges.claim: Venus is grouped with Mercury and the Moon at the metabolic-limb pole.
edges.qualification: There is no exclusive one-to-one pairing in this passage.

edges.context: Planetary activity in the threefold body
edges.claim: Mercury is grouped with Venus and the Moon at the metabolic-limb pole.
edges.qualification: The same source relates bodily form to zodiacal constellations.

edges.context: Planetary activity in the threefold body
edges.claim: The Moon is grouped with Mercury and Venus at the metabolic-limb pole.
edges.qualification: Reproduction is singled out in the same paragraph.

edges.claim: The Lemurian condition precedes Steiner’s Atlantean differentiation of human consciousness.
edges.qualification: Use as a sequence within the esoteric narrative.

edges.claim: Steiner portrays early Atlanteans as relying on vivid memory and speech before increasingly independent logical thought.
edges.qualification: These are textual claims about his narrative, not archaeological observations.

edges.claim: Oracle schools cultivate distinct forms of initiation in Steiner’s Atlantean narrative.
edges.qualification: The number and status of the Sun and Vulcan centers are discussed separately.

edges.claim: The first phase is characterized by retention of vivid sensory impressions and development of speech with formative power.
edges.qualification: The stage numbering is editorial. Steiner uses obsolete Theosophical racial terminology.

edges.claim: The second phase adds a sense of personal value and memory of actions that win recognition.
edges.qualification: The text links these changes with the beginnings of communal remembrance.

edges.claim: Steiner makes remembered personal experience, tradition and continuity of leadership more important in the third phase.
edges.qualification: This is his account of early political organization.

edges.claim: The fourth phase uses inherited capacities for selfish ends, to which Steiner connects destructive effects.
edges.qualification: GA 13 IV also discusses misuse of growth and reproductive forces at the level of Atlantis as a whole.

edges.claim: The fifth phase develops an inner basis for decisions through thought and checks the dominance of personal desire.
edges.qualification: Steiner depicts the transition as a shift of motive into the individual.

edges.claim: The sixth phase uses thinking more extensively for social rules and wider collective organization.
edges.qualification: This is the conceptual change described in GA 11.

edges.claim: Steiner combines developing thought with a stronger retention of earlier traits in the seventh phase.
edges.qualification: No application of his racial labels to living peoples is warranted.

edges.claim: The preservers of initiation and the seven teachers connect Atlantis to Steiner’s Ancient Indian epoch.
edges.qualification: In GA 13 the teacher appoints seven disciples. GA 109 supplies the name Manu.

edges.claim: The First Post-Atlantean account describes surviving older supersensible perception. Atlantean continuity is an interpretive link across the passages.
edges.qualification: The term picture-consciousness is broader in other Steiner contexts.

edges.claim: Steiner describes a turn toward shaping the sensory world under the instruction of ancient Persian culture.
edges.qualification: The same chapter distinguishes the esoteric Zarathustra from simple historical identification.

edges.claim: Steiner describes a search for spiritual laws within sensory appearance, including star observation in the third period.
edges.qualification: The zodiac node identifies the broader astral study route.

edges.claim: Steiner relates greater investment in sensory earthly life to consolidation of intellect and feeling.
edges.qualification: The use of the intellectual soul as a graph connection is editorial.

edges.claim: The fifth epoch develops independent engagement with sensory knowledge and the conditions for renewed awareness of spirit.
edges.qualification: GA 102 III locates the first stirrings of the consciousness soul much earlier, late in Atlantis.

edges.claim: Steiner projects a further reconciliation of life in the spirit with material culture and voluntary conscious perception.
edges.qualification: The sixth epoch is a subdivision of Earth evolution.

edges.claim: A major transition follows the seventh cultural period and opens a new series of earthly conditions.
edges.qualification: GA 13 provides a transition marker. A separate detailed seventh-period profile remains open.

edges.claim: Steiner describes Spirits of Personality teaching and guiding in the Lemurian narrative through beings from the Venus sphere.
edges.qualification: The esoteric Venus terminology is the one explained in the lecture.

edges.claim: Steiner brings Mercury spirits and Archangels into his later account of Atlantean leadership.
edges.qualification: The passage uses the esoteric Mercury terminology.

edges.claim: The first lunar passage confronts the dead with their moral character and the primeval teachers.
edges.qualification: GA 108 separately describes the period of releasing desires. An exact concordance of all its phases with GA 231 remains open.

edges.claim: Understanding of what had previously been perceived starts to develop as the dead encounter the Third Hierarchy.
edges.qualification: This is an experience of several ranks, while GA 110 draws a single boundary marker for Archangeloi.

edges.claim: The dead encounter cosmic love in Venus existence. The sphere works especially on the will.
edges.qualification: Steiner describes the response as depending on capacities brought from life on Earth.

edges.claim: The dead experience cosmic harmony in the Sun sphere.
edges.qualification: GA 231 III also associates this solar stage with feeling and the Second Hierarchy.

edges.claim: Cosmic music becomes cosmic speech in the Mars region.
edges.qualification: GA 228 gives a parallel Mars speech motif in a different frame.

edges.claim: Jupiter’s spiritual beings guard and radiate cosmic thoughts, which the human being encounters.
edges.qualification: This is part of the metamorphosis leading toward the head germ of another incarnation.

edges.claim: The person encounters the planetary system’s cosmic memory in the Saturn sphere.
edges.qualification: Compare the Saturn memory description in GA 228.

edges.claim: On return through Saturn, cosmic memory becomes the germ of the future human faculty of memory.
edges.qualification: Steiner distinguishes outward experience and return transformation.

edges.claim: On return through Jupiter, perceived cosmic thoughts are transformed into a germ of earthly thinking.
edges.qualification: The change is linked to the spiritual germ of the head.

edges.claim: On return through Mars, participation in the cosmic Word is linked to the germ of human speech.
edges.qualification: The same paragraph also names chest and limb germs.

edges.claim: Steiner assigns the addition of new spiritual limb and breast-system germs to the Mars passage.
edges.qualification: He explicitly places this on a spiritual level.

edges.claim: Steiner jointly places implantation of additional organ germs at the passages through Venus and Mercury.
edges.qualification: He gives no organ-by-organ assignment here.

edges.claim: Mercury and Venus are both named in the passage on other organ germs.
edges.qualification: This does not independently prove that Mercury supplies lung germs.

edges.claim: The account puts the return lunar passage alongside the earthly interval between conception and birth.
edges.qualification: This is an esoteric parallel with embryonic development.

edges.claim: Steiner characterizes Saturn’s way of shaping karma through a relation to the past and intense effects in the soul.
edges.qualification: GA 239’s historical incarnation identifications are claims of its lecture context.

edges.claim: Steiner places Exusiai, Dynamis and Kyriotetes in the Sun sphere in accounts of the interval between lives.
edges.qualification: The Sun includes several hierarchies in this account.

edges.claim: Steiner argues that people carry effects of earlier historical conditions into later epochs through reincarnation.
edges.qualification: The claim belongs to his esoteric account of history.

edges.claim: Sun-sphere forces act particularly on what appears on Earth as feeling.
edges.qualification: GA 209 associates feeling with rhythm in embodied life through a different explanatory route.

edges.claim: Gabriel is named with the lunar planetary intelligence.
edges.qualification: Jehovah’s association with the Moon belongs to a different hierarchy and lecture context.

edges.claim: Raphael is named with the Mercury intelligence.
edges.qualification: Follow the naming recorded in this lecture.

edges.claim: Anael is named with the Venus intelligence.
edges.qualification: This is an Archangelic administration.

edges.claim: Michael primarily administers the solar intelligence and presides over the planetary administrators.
edges.qualification: Steiner explicitly describes shared administration under Michael.

edges.claim: Samael is named with the Mars intelligence.
edges.qualification: This is separate from the domain boundary of the Dynamis.

edges.claim: Zachariel is named with the Jupiter intelligence in this edition.
edges.qualification: The graph preserves the edition’s spelling.

edges.claim: Oriphiel is named with the Saturn intelligence.
edges.qualification: The Thrones’ assignment is a distinct relationship.

edges.claim: The Sun Oracle is portrayed as a central site where the wisdom of seven Oracle streams comes together.
edges.qualification: The status of the secretly preparing Vulcan Oracle requires separate accounting.

edges.claim: The Vulcan Oracle prepares in secrecy, while GA 13 associates its stream with earthly phenomena.
edges.qualification: The projected Future Vulcan is a different type of entity.

edges.claim: Steiner links specialists of this Oracle with earthly experience and early arts and sciences.
edges.qualification: He locates the Oracle’s guide in the Earth’s environment and assigns it no planet of its own.

edges.claim: Steiner identifies Manu as the leader who preserves the tradition and chooses people whose older clairvoyance is waning.
edges.qualification: Steiner states that the name is less important than the function.

edges.claim: The initiate sends seven teachers who continue differentiated Atlantean wisdom in the first Post-Atlantean epoch.
edges.qualification: GA 109 explains continuity through preserved etheric organizations in its doctrine of spiritual economy.

edges.claim: The highest Sun Being works on the Rishis from outside. Their high perception reaches the being as a distant spiritual source.
edges.qualification: In the narrative, the limitation concerns form of access and evolutionary timing.

edges.claim: Steiner identifies Vishva Karman with the Rishis’ designation for the elevated spiritual source.
edges.qualification: This records Steiner’s comparative theology.

edges.claim: For Steiner, Zarathustra recognizes the spiritual Sun behind the visible one as Ahura Mazda.
edges.qualification: The comparison in GA 113 distinguishes this mode of access from ancient Indian perception.

edges.claim: Steiner names Osiris in his sequence of ways the Christ Being was known in mystery traditions.
edges.qualification: This is his esoteric reading of those traditions.

edges.claim: The early Christianizing mystery account sometimes uses identity language for Yahweh and Christ. The hierarchy lecture identifies Jehovah as the lunar Elohim.
edges.qualification: Whether the identity is meant as manifestation, mediation or a stronger identity needs further comparison.

edges.claim: Steiner describes Christ’s union with Earth through Golgotha, using the motif of the blood shed there.
edges.qualification: Compare the separate physiology of blood and I in GA 107.

edges.claim: Steiner presents the exalted Sun Being as the archetype of love, whose seed is placed in human nature.
edges.qualification: Earth adds love to the wisdom inherited from earlier evolution.

edges.claim: Steiner connects Christ’s spiritual warmth with activity that makes freedom possible and assigns the originating free deed to the I.
edges.qualification: He distinguishes GA 4’s philosophical route from the spiritual experience described here.

edges.claim: Michael’s work is brought into harmony with the Mystery of Golgotha in the world age of human freedom.
edges.qualification: Michael is named as an Archangel. The Christ relation is stated at another theological level.

edges.claim: GA 4 treats moral intuition and love of the deed as sources of free action. GA 26 attributes the free to the human I.
edges.qualification: GA 26 explicitly distinguishes the basis of GA 4 from spiritual experience of Michael.

edges.claim: Steiner places the Luciferic intervention in human astral development and connects it with independence and vulnerability to error.
edges.qualification: The account gives the intervention mixed consequences.

edges.claim: Steiner connects Ahrimanic influence with an increasingly misleading grasp of sensory existence and with consequences beyond death.
edges.qualification: The Luciferic and Ahrimanic accounts overlap in their effects but are differentiated.

edges.claim: Steiner treats the historical descent of Christ as a prerequisite for the later possibility of an inward mystical Christ experience.
edges.qualification: This is the lecture’s specific account of why modes of revelation change.

edges.claim: Steiner relates Aries, Taurus, Gemini and Cancer to head formation.
edges.qualification: GA 209 distinguishes the formative zodiac from the planetary activity emphasized in §31.

edges.claim: Steiner relates Leo, Virgo, Libra and Scorpio to the chest organization.
edges.qualification: This is a fourfold group within the zodiacal twelve.

edges.claim: Steiner assigns the remaining zodiacal group an action upon limb form.
edges.qualification: The source portrays action from beneath Earth.

edges.claim: The twelvefold fixed-star framework is used to discuss bodily form, alongside a planetary framework for bodily activities.
edges.qualification: This is one lecture cycle’s distinction.

edges.claim: Steiner links the Aries imagery of looking back with self-contemplation in the Greek epoch.
edges.qualification: The correspondence is part of his esoteric reading of the vernal point and human culture.

edges.claim: The present sphere has a spatial function in GA 110; Future Jupiter is a later condition of Earth evolution.
edges.qualification: Shared labels establish neither identity nor automatic causation.

edges.claim: Vulcan names both an Atlantean oracle tradition and a later claim about approaching spiritual beings.
edges.qualification: The sources examined do not establish continuity of personnel.

edges.claim: The hidden Oracle and the future embodiment belong to different scales.
edges.qualification: A typological connection remains a question for further work.

edges.claim: Steiner explicitly interchanges contemporary and esoteric Mercury and Venus labels in GA 110.
edges.qualification: Apply this declaration to its own context. Normalize other texts only after their wording and frame are independently established.

edges.claim: In one lecture, §22 names Venus beings for intellectuality and §§23–24 name Mercury in the formation of the intellectual soul.
edges.qualification: The distinction between intellectuality and a soul member may matter. Neither a translation error nor a typographical fix is established.

edges.claim: Saturn influence on the liver and the Jovian liver image both survive source checking.
edges.qualification: Their predicates and lecture purposes differ. A full explanation of their overlap is open.

edges.context: Hierarchy boundary and several solar ranks
edges.claim: GA 110 draws a solar boundary for Exusiai, GA 231 describes a meeting place of the Second Hierarchy and GA 237 names Michael’s administration.
edges.qualification: The three passages specify different kinds of relation.

edges.claim: The Mercury boundary is associated with Archangels in GA 110. GA 231 describes beings of all three Third Hierarchy ranks in Mercury existence.
edges.qualification: The distinction is useful for reading the two statements together.

edges.context: Christ, the Sun and the lunar Elohim
edges.claim: GA 113 speaks of Yahweh and Christ as one in different forms. GA 121 separately assigns the lunar Elohim a cooperative task.
edges.qualification: The evidence supports retaining both statements. The full doctrinal reconciliation is open.

edges.claim: GA 102 dates first stirring of the consciousness soul late in Atlantis. GA 13 discusses the much later fifth epoch’s cultivation of independently acquired knowledge.
edges.qualification: A first emergence and a later cultural emphasis are different chronological claims.

edges.claim: GA 109 describes seven Oracle capacities converging at the Sun center and Vulcan preparing in secrecy. GA 13 narrates several branches with distinct initiation histories.
edges.qualification: A definitive reconciled count requires comparing the German and other accounts of Oracle organization.

edges.claim: Steiner traces glandular beginnings to the activity of the Spirits of Love with the Spirits of Personality on Old Sun.
edges.qualification: GA 107 separately associates the already formed glandular system with the etheric body.

edges.claim: Steiner describes the Cherubim imparting vision to the Angels, who work its imagery into the human etheric body.
edges.qualification: This is a later contribution within Old Sun, alongside the earlier activity of Spirits of Wisdom.

edges.claim: Steiner attributes the first sense-organ germs in warmth and their further working to the Fire Spirits.
edges.qualification: The early germs do not yet perform Earth-style perception.

edges.claim: On return through Mars, Steiner explicitly places the addition of spiritual germs for the larynx and lung formations.
edges.qualification: This is distinct from Mercury as the pulmonary image in GA 128.

edges.claim: Steiner ascribes glandular beginnings to the Spirits of Personality working with the Seraphim.
edges.qualification: There is no claim of an exclusive present-day planetary source.

edges.claim: The lung system is imaged as Mercury in occult physiology and has a spiritual germ added on the Mars return in GA 231.
edges.qualification: Their distinct predicates preserve both source claims without an identification.

edges.claim: Steiner connects early bodily differentiation with changes in reproductive organization and the increasing inward use of life forces.
edges.qualification: The esoteric account is not historical evidence about human origins or a biological explanation of sex.

edges.claim: Steiner approaches a shared divine origin through nature and through the inner experience of moral ideals.
edges.qualification: The first lecture introduces the two approaches without assigning a planet to moral ideals.

edges.claim: The lecture proposes imagining a person whose aims and faculties correspond to events that appear accidental.
edges.qualification: The exercise is an approach Steiner proposes to karma, not a way to establish a particular incarnation historically.

edges.claim: Earth’s independent I remains a starting point as the higher human members unfold in the projected future.
edges.qualification: GA 13 frames love as an added activity of the I. GA 103 treats the transformation of its lower members.

edges.claim: The experience of the macrocosmic heart is compared with the sense of being bound up with bodily heartbeat.
edges.qualification: The passage compares the experiences and works across two different settings.

edges.claim: The heart belongs to the circulatory system Steiner calls Sun-like. Blood is separately named as an expression of the I, and GA 13 links its first tendencies with warmth.
edges.qualification: The bridge brings these contexts together without assigning a single mechanism.

edges.context: Christ and the bodily expression of the I
edges.claim: Steiner uses blood at Golgotha in the Christ narrative and blood as the physical expression of the I in the constitution narrative.
edges.qualification: An explicit doctrine connecting all these passages still needs closer inquiry.

edges.claim: Steiner describes Hermes preparing Egyptians during life for companionship with the Spirit of Light beyond death.
edges.qualification: This is Steiner’s mystery-history account.

edges.claim: Steiner groups the spleen, liver and gallbladder in the inner transformation of nourishment.
edges.qualification: The lecture goes on to describe reciprocal interactions with the organs of a different functional group.
